what: Hook system — IMPLEMENTED. 6 hooks total, session-scoped recall tracking. (1) Read (PreToolUse:Read): shows layer breakdown + topic keywords, BLOCKS first read per path per session until aide_recall called, soft nudge after. (2) Track recall (PreToolUse:mcp__aide-memory__aide_recall): writes recalled paths to session-scoped file (.aide/cache/recalled-paths-{session_id}.txt). All tracking in hooks, not MCP server — key insight: PreToolUse can match MCP tool calls (mcp__server__tool pattern). (3) SessionStart: cleans up stale tracking files from other sessions. (4) Stop: blocks, prompts aide_remember. (5) UserPromptSubmit: blocks on corrections/decisions/preferences. (6) PreCompact: blocks + clears current session's recalled-paths file (agent loses context on compaction, must re-recall). session_id is available in hook stdin JSON but NOT as env var for MCP servers (feature request anthropics/claude-code#25642). That's why tracking moved from MCP server to hooks.
why: PreCompact must clear session tracking because compaction drops tool results from context. session_id availability distinction (hooks vs env var) was the key design constraint — earlier attempts to track in MCP server failed because session_id isn't exposed to child processes.
